title: Quiz — Chapter 5.7: Systems of Linear Inequalities

questions.prompt: What is a solution of a system of linear inequalities?
options: A. Any ordered pair that satisfies at least one inequality
B. An ordered pair that satisfies all inequalities in the system
C. The intersection point of the boundary lines
D. Any point on a boundary line
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A solution must satisfy all inequalities in the system.
hints: It must work for every inequality.
Think of multiple conditions that must all be met.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The graph is the intersection (or overlap) of the individual graphs.
questions.prompt: The graph of a system of linear inequalities is the ___ of the graphs of the individual inequalities.
hints: It's the region common to all shaded parts.
Think of where all the shadings meet.

questions.prompt: Is the ordered pair (3, 5) a solution of the system y < 2x and y ≥ x + 1? (yes/no)

hints: No overlap means no point is in all shaded regions.
Think of parallel lines with opposite shadings.
questions.prompt: A system of linear inequalities has no solution when:
options: B. The shaded half-planes do not overlap
D. The boundary lines are dashed
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The system has no solution when the half-planes do not overlap.
The line y = 3 is solid because the inequality is ≤.
questions.prompt: For the system y ≤ 3 and y > x + 2, the boundary line y = 3 is ___ (solid/dashed).
Graph the system: y ≥ -x + 4 and x + y ≤ 0. Is the origin (0, 0) in the solution region? (yes/no)
Which system of inequalities is represented by a solid horizontal line y = -2 shaded above, and a dashed line y = x shaded below?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The system is y ≥ -2 and y < x.

questions.prompt: A graph shows a solid vertical line x = 3 with shading to the left. The inequality is x ___ 3.
You can spend at most $21 on blueberries ($4/lb) and strawberries ($3/lb). You need at least 3 pounds total. Write the budget inequality. (Use x for blueberries, y for strawberries)
In the mall/beach problem (x + y ≤ 8, x ≥ 2, y > 4), which point is a solution?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: (3, 5) satisfies all constraints. The others fail at least one.

questions.prompt: In the system x + y ≤ 10 and x - y ≥ 2, the boundary line for the first inequality is ___ (solid/dashed).
A system has boundary lines y = 2x - 3 and y = 2x + 1. If the first inequality is y < 2x - 3 (shade below) and the second is y > 2x + 1 (shade above), how many solutions does the system have?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: No solution, because the half-planes never intersect.
hints: The shaded regions do not overlap.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The total hours constraint is x + y ≤ 20.
questions.prompt: You earn $10/h as a manager (min 8 h/wk) and $15/h teaching. You need at least $120/wk and work at most 20 h/wk. Which inequality represents the total hours constraint?
In the work problem, the minimum earnings constraint of 'at least $120 per week' is modeled by 10x + 15y ___ 120.
hints: 'At least' means greater than or equal.
Use the symbol with the line under it.

questions.prompt: Is the point (4, -3) a solution of the system y ≤ -x + 1 and y ≤ 5x - 2? (yes/no)
